merged_threads.description:

reconciled_statuses.description:
Delivery statuses reconciled in place from sent list metadata;
always zero for the inbound direction.

outbound.description: One direction's share of a completed sync run.

anyOf.description:
Sanitized, resumable failure state for one mailbox direction. Persisted
as JSON in `mailbox_sync_state.failure_json`; carries provider ids and an
error class only — never secrets, URLs, or raw provider payloads.

merged_threads.description:
RFC-proven thread merges performed by imported outbound roots;
always zero for the inbound direction.

reconciled_statuses.description:
Delivery statuses reconciled in place from sent list metadata;
always zero for the inbound direction.

pending_triage.description:
一个收件箱欠下的判断:有界的清单加上真实总数,免得积压很多时把
返回撑爆,又不至于让被截断的部分看起来不存在。

items.description:
一条还欠着判断的入站消息:同步把它收进来了,但没有人——也没有
agent——说过它是什么意思。

它跟着同步结果一起返回,因为提醒放在指令里只是请求,放在返回值里
就是事实:agent 必然读到工具调用的结果,而这份清单要么是空的,要么
明摆着还有活没干。判断完再同步一次,清单自己会空掉。

channel.description: Which inbox the judged reply arrived in.

from.description: 发信人,足够让 agent 认出这是谁而不必再取一次。

total.description: 全部欠着的条数,可能大于 items.len()。

output_schema.title: MailboxSyncOutcome

metadata.summary: Read the latest local sync status for one connected mailbox.
metadata.title: Get mailbox sync status

output_schema.description:
Idle-time status: whether a run is in flight in this process plus the
durable per-direction facts. Process-only running state stays separate
from durable watermarks by construction.

anyOf.description:
Public projection of one direction's durable sync state. Deliberately
omits provider pagination positions (`newest_provider_message_id`,
`oldest_backfill_cursor`): those are private engine state, not status.

Sanitized, resumable failure state for one mailbox direction. Persisted
as JSON in `mailbox_sync_state.failure_json`; carries provider ids and an
error class only — never secrets, URLs, or raw provider payloads.

Public projection of one direction's durable sync state. Deliberately
omits provider pagination positions (`newest_provider_message_id`,
`oldest_backfill_cursor`): those are private engine state, not status.

Sanitized, resumable failure state for one mailbox direction. Persisted
as JSON in `mailbox_sync_state.failure_json`; carries provider ids and an
error class only — never secrets, URLs, or raw provider payloads.

Live counters of an in-flight run: the direction currently walking and
what this run has listed, fetched, and imported so far. Process-local by
construction — never durable state, never provider cursors — and reset
per direction, so the UI reads "which phase, how far".

estimated_percent.description:
Estimated share (0–100) of the backfill window already walked. The
provider exposes no total count, but the walk moves newest→oldest
through a bounded retention window, so elapsed time-span is an
honest determinate estimate. Absent when no page boundary is known.

progress.description: Present only while `running`: the in-flight run's live counters.

anyOf.description:
List-row projection of one email message: routing facts plus a bounded

The verdict as an inbox row shows it: enough for a tag and a hover, not

intent.description:
What an inbound reply is actually asking for. Six values, chosen so a
human scanning a list can act on the tag alone: three that want a reply
now, one that closes the thread, one that is noise, and an escape hatch
so an agent is never forced to mislabel.

oneOf.description: Wants to work together; the next move is ours.
Needs something answered before deciding.
Discussing terms — price, scope, timing.
Said no. The thread is closed unless something changes.
Auto-reply, unrelated, or spam.
Real but none of the above; the summary carries the meaning.

triage.description:
The newest verdict on any inbound message of this thread — newest by
when it was judged, not by which message it judges. A later inbound
that nobody has read yet leaves the earlier verdict standing here;
what is still owed is `pending_triage` on the sync result, not the
absence of this field.

pending_triage.description:
这条会话里还欠着判断的入站消息。与邮箱同步同一笔账:收进来是
一半,说清楚每条是什么意思是另一半。

items.description:
一条还欠着判断的入站消息:同步把它收进来了,但没有人——也没有
agent——说过它是什么意思。

它跟着同步结果一起返回,因为提醒放在指令里只是请求,放在返回值里
就是事实:agent 必然读到工具调用的结果,而这份清单要么是空的,要么
明摆着还有活没干。判断完再同步一次,清单自己会空掉。

channel.description: Which inbox the judged reply arrived in.

from.description: 发信人,足够让 agent 认出这是谁而不必再取一次。

total.description: 全部欠着的条数,可能大于 items.len()。

query.description:
Case-insensitive substring match on the Creator display name, the
peer's latest observed handle, or the operator-account label. A leading
'@' is ignored.

anyOf.description:
Bounded, filterable inbox page over locally persisted DM conversations,
newest activity first.

status.description:
Reply state derived from the latest persisted message direction. DM
providers do not expose a reliable read/unread state.

output_schema.description:
One bounded page of summary items from a local list read.

`next_cursor` is present only when more items exist; it is opaque and
bound to the issuing query context, so it cannot be replayed against a
different filter set or resource.

items.description:
One DM-inbox row: the persisted conversation plus the full four-id route
context the desktop needs to open its thread directly, and the fields the
list line renders. Local data only.

creator_avatar_url.description:
The creator's display avatar (first-captured account first, falling
back to the next account that has one) — the same face everywhere
this person appears, not a per-thread one.

peer_handle.description: Latest observed handle of that peer account.

anyOf.description:
The verdict as an inbox row shows it: enough for a tag and a hover, not
the whole record.

intent.description:
What an inbound reply is actually asking for. Six values, chosen so a
human scanning a list can act on the tag alone: three that want a reply
now, one that closes the thread, one that is noise, and an escape hatch
so an agent is never forced to mislabel.

oneOf.description: Wants to work together; the next move is ours.
Needs something answered before deciding.
Discussing terms — price, scope, timing.
Said no. The thread is closed unless something changes.
Auto-reply, unrelated, or spam.
Real but none of the above; the summary carries the meaning.

triage.description:
The newest verdict on any inbound message of this conversation —
newest by when it was judged, not by which message it judges. A later
unread inbound leaves the earlier verdict standing; what is still owed
is `pending_triage`. It belongs on the row because that is where a
human decides what to open next.

output_schema.title: Page

operation's arguments; changed provider criteria require a new plan.

metadata.summary: Confirm external creator/content search criteria and keywords; no provider call or persisted plan. output_schema.description:
One agent verdict about one inbound message. Recording a second verdict
for the same message replaces the first: a message has one current
reading, not a history of guesses.

channel.description: Which inbox the judged reply arrived in.

intent.description:
What an inbound reply is actually asking for. Six values, chosen so a
human scanning a list can act on the tag alone: three that want a reply
now, one that closes the thread, one that is noise, and an escape hatch
so an agent is never forced to mislabel.

oneOf.description: Wants to work together; the next move is ours.
Needs something answered before deciding.
Discussing terms — price, scope, timing.
Said no. The thread is closed unless something changes.
Auto-reply, unrelated, or spam.
Real but none of the above; the summary carries the meaning.

suggested_reply.description:
Drafted wording the human can adopt or edit. Absent when the intent
does not call for a reply.

summary.description: Why the agent read it that way, in one or two sentences.

metadata.summary: Start, inspect, complete, or cancel one visible Instagram browser login.
metadata.title: Connect an Instagram Operator

recommended_steps.instruction: Start the Instagram browser login with its selected proxy.
Complete the visible provider login, polling bounded status when needed.
Confirm completion only after the browser interaction succeeds.
Cancel the same operation if the attended login will not continue.

entries.use_case: Connect one Instagram operator account through the attended browser lifecycle.

metadata.summary: Search Instagram accounts and inspect one profile with Instagram-specific identifiers only for a decision-changing evidence gap.
metadata.title: Find Creators on Instagram

recommended_steps.instruction: Search Instagram accounts by keyword.
Use returned account evidence first; inspect one selected profile only for one decision-changing gap, never as a mechanical prefetch.

entries.use_case: Find relevant Instagram accounts and inspect a selected profile only for a decision-changing evidence gap.

known_pitfalls: Use the batch operation for more than one candidate; do not repeat onecrew.creator.candidate.save.
No Creator is persisted before explicit route confirmation.

metadata.summary: Prepare several selected candidates together, review their contact routes in one batch card, confirm selected rows, and read back the saved Creators.
metadata.title: Save Creator Candidates in a Batch

recommended_steps.instruction: Fetch the current batch-save input contract and pass one candidates array with one consistent explicit intent plus target, connection, real provenance, notes, tags and quality per candidate; present the returned result_ref review.
The user confirms selected rows and contact routes through the App-only onecrew_result_state action confirm_creator_save_batch, then read back each saved Creator.

entries.use_case: Save multiple selected accounts through one OneCrew batch payload. The business batch supports up to 50 candidates; it is separate from the eight-call MCP transport envelope and provider-read concurrency.

known_pitfalls: Original discovery and candidate IDs are provenance, not cache keys. Preparation writes no Creator rows or reservations. Follow actual row_id values through the review and outcome.

metadata.summary: Prepare and confirm saving one selected platform account as a Creator, then read it back.
metadata.title: Save One Creator Candidate

recommended_steps.instruction: Use the current candidate-save input contract to pass the explicit per-candidate intent, target, connection, real provenance, notes, tags and quality directly; do not add a save-only prefetch; present the returned result_ref for review.
The user confirms rows and routes through the App-only onecrew_result_state action confirm_creator_save_batch; read back the saved Creator after completion.

entries.use_case: Save one selected platform target directly: let preparation obtain fresh platform data, review contact routes, confirm in the App and read back the Creator.

known_pitfalls: Do not confirm an unverified route merely because it was discovered.

metadata.summary: Prepare fresh profile and link-hub data directly from a saved Creator's verified platform locator and explicitly confirm contact routes before treating them as durable facts.
metadata.title: Confirm Creator Contact

recommended_steps.instruction: Pass the verified locator, connection and real provenance directly using the current save contract. The runtime reads fresh profile and link-hub data; present the returned result_ref and inspect the identity resolution and offered routes.
The user confirms only selected rows and routes in the App, then read back the Creator after completion.

entries.use_case: Prepare a fresh review from the selected locator, then confirm selected routes through the App.

known_pitfalls: Send the complete items array in one operation; do not emit one onecrew.creator.manual.create call per row.
Set confirmed to true only when the user has authorized the complete batch.
Use strict validation when every row must pass, and permissive validation when deterministic invalid rows may be reported individually.

metadata.summary: Create up to 50 explicit manual Creators from one confirmed payload and verify the persisted Creator records.
metadata.title: Create Manual Creators in a Batch

recommended_steps.instruction: Map explicit Creator rows into one batch payload with a stable idempotency key.
Read back each accepted Creator from the authoritative Creator projection.

entries.use_case: Use onecrew.creator.batch.create once with the complete items array. The 50-item business limit is independent of the eight-call onecrew_tool_execute transport envelope.

known_pitfalls: Avatar, handle, bio and homepage changes are observations, not Creator update fields; save the same account again through onecrew.creator.candidate.save to append them.

metadata.summary: Read the platform profile, write the Creator fields the user explicitly chose, and verify the authoritative Creator projection.
metadata.title: Update a Creator Profile

recommended_steps.instruction: Read the account's platform-native profile with its platform profile or channel get, such as x.profile.get, instagram.profile.get or youtube.channel.get; the read writes no Creator data.
Write only the follower count or display name the user explicitly chose.
Read back the authoritative Creator projection.

entries.use_case: Update a saved Creator's follower count or display name from a separate platform read, then read back its Creator projection.

metadata.summary: Search Instagram, inspect candidates, then save one selected candidate as a Creator.
metadata.title: Find and Save Instagram Creators

recommended_steps.instruction: Search Instagram accounts and retain selected account locators and original source metadata.

Apply the user's original request and confirmed criteria. Distinguish matched, unmatched and unverified; group hits by each platform's stable identity, retain every source, and never merge same names across platforms.

Continue without an extra profile read when evidence suffices. Reuse reads by connection, operation revision, params, depth and cursor. Read once per decision-changing gap; if still unknown, stop. Follow the live workflow guide.

Retrieve the shared grade rubric from the live find-batch workflow guide; keep match separate from grade and write an individual evidence-based reason. Stop when the match target is met; use the returned cursor for an approved next page.

Use explicit add_new by default, or save_or_update only when requested; pass the exact locator, tagged connection, real provenance, quality and intent. Prepare gets fresh data, does not write or auto-confirm; present result_ref and wait.
After the user confirms the reviewed rows in the App, read back each saved Creator; preparation does not write.

entries.use_case: Search Instagram, inspect candidates, then save one selected candidate as a Creator.

metadata.title: Triage Email into OneCrew

recommended_steps.instruction: Sync the mailbox and list its current canonical threads.
Record one OneCrew triage verdict per inbound reply.
Read back the durable triage state before deciding it is resolved.
Acknowledge the durable reminder only after the resolved verdict is verified.

entries.use_case: Sync email, record one OneCrew verdict per reply, and acknowledge the durable reminder when resolved.

known_pitfalls: Telegram community search has no continuation cursor and creates no Creator snapshots.

metadata.summary: Search Telegram communities and preserve the provider's public chat IDs and kinds.
metadata.title: Find Telegram Communities

recommended_steps.instruction: Search Telegram communities by keyword.
Review the native public chat objects and select their exact IDs and kinds.

entries.use_case: Find Telegram communities relevant to a topic.

known_pitfalls: Never log, persist, or reuse OTP and two-factor values.

metadata.summary: Start and monitor Telegram phone login, submit OTP and possible 2FA, or cancel the operation.
metadata.title: Connect Telegram by Phone

recommended_steps.instruction: Start Telegram with method=phone, E.164 phone, and the required SOCKS5 proxy.
Poll status only until the projected operation expiry.
Submit the OTP and, only if requested, the two-factor password through their transient fields.
Cancel the same operation when the attended flow will not continue.

entries.use_case: Connect one Telegram operator account through the phone, OTP, and 2FA continuation lifecycle.

known_pitfalls: Do not substitute phone login or expose the QR token outside its rendered handoff.

metadata.summary: Start and monitor a Telegram QR login, including a possible 2FA continuation and cancellation.
metadata.title: Connect Telegram by QR

recommended_steps.instruction: Start Telegram with method=qr and the required SOCKS5 proxy.
Poll status only until the projected operation expiry.
If status requests 2FA, submit it only through the transient secret field.
Cancel the same operation when the QR flow expires or is abandoned.

entries.use_case: Connect one Telegram operator account with QR login and bounded continuation handling.

known_pitfalls: Never reuse an Instagram operation ID or submit an X Chat passcode through another toolkit.

metadata.summary: Start, inspect, complete, or cancel one visible X browser login.
metadata.title: Connect an X Operator

recommended_steps.instruction: Start the X browser login with its selected proxy and X Chat preference.
Complete the visible provider login, polling bounded status when needed.
Confirm completion only after the browser interaction succeeds.
Cancel the same operation if the attended login will not continue.

entries.use_case: Connect one X operator account through the attended browser lifecycle.

known_pitfalls: Use the returned X handle; do not substitute another platform identifier.

metadata.summary: Find X creators through advanced post search, deduplicate matching authors, and inspect profiles or recent posts only when the requested quality evidence is missing.
metadata.title: Discover X Authors Through Matching Posts

recommended_steps.instruction: Search X posts with typed advanced criteria.
Deduplicate matching authors by stable X identity and keep every source; use search evidence first, then inspect one profile or recent-post page only for one decision-changing gap.

entries.use_case: Find X creator accounts through matching posts and inspect public profiles only when search results lack the requested quality evidence.

known_pitfalls: Carry the exact post locator returned by X search.

metadata.summary: Locate X posts and read the thread for a selected post.
metadata.title: Read an X Thread

recommended_steps.instruction: Search X posts with typed advanced criteria.
Read the selected post thread.

entries.use_case: Find an X post and read its conversation thread.

known_pitfalls: Search items retain channel_id; pass next_page_token as cursor. youtube.channel.get accepts a channel ID, not a handle.

metadata.summary: Search YouTube channels and deduplicate stable channel IDs. Connection and read depth identify equivalent reads. Inspect a channel only for a decision-changing quality evidence gap; pass depth: light or full; light omits comments.
metadata.title: Find YouTube Channels

recommended_steps.instruction: Search YouTube channels by keyword.

Deduplicate hits by stable channel ID, not connection or depth; those identify equivalent reads. Continue without an extra channel read when evidence suffices; read one channel for one decision-changing gap at depth: light or full.

entries.use_case: Discover YouTube channels and inspect one channel when quality evidence is missing; preserve every hit's source.

known_pitfalls: A successful local connection does not imply unlimited YouTube quota or provider entitlement.

metadata.summary: Connect, inspect, rename, rotate, or delete one YouTube API credential through its typed lifecycle.
metadata.title: Manage a YouTube Credential

recommended_steps.instruction: Connect the API key and retain the returned credential ID.
Inspect that exact credential before choosing a mutation.
Rename or rotate the same credential without translating its ID.
Delete only the confirmed selected credential.

entries.use_case: Manage one YouTube service credential while retaining its opaque credential ID.

output_schema.description: One live self-check of a connection.

account_handle.description: The signed-in account handle; present only when the provider accepted the session.

checked_at.description: Unix seconds when the check finished.

country.description: Country reported by the IP-echo service; empty when unknown.

egress.description: The configured proxy's observed exit; present only when that proxy answered.

proxy_configured.description: Whether provider traffic for this connection routes through a configured proxy.

oneOf.description: The network, the proxy when configured, and the provider all accepted the connection.

The configured proxy did not answer or cannot carry this provider, or a provider that
requires a proxy has none; the provider was not called.
The provider could not be reached from this computer or through its proxy (no HTTP response).
The provider rejected the stored session or key; reconnect the account or replace the key.
The provider answered with a server error, a rate limit, or an unexpected response.

output_schema.title: ConnectionCheck

Provider-aware instructions shown immediately before browser completion.

provider.description:
Runtime-owned cookie acquisition contract. Adapters must project this value
and must not infer provider behavior from the host OS themselves.

cookie_provider.description:
Runtime-owned cookie acquisition contract. Adapters must project this value
and must not infer provider behavior from the host OS themselves.

anyOf.description:
Stable public error codes for capability gates. Human-readable detection or
provider failures remain in `limitations` and are never substituted for the
machine-readable code.

os.description: Desktop operating system relevant to the browser-login capability.

path.description: Absolute path to the resolved Chrome binary (for display), if found.

state.description: End-to-end state of browser login, rather than merely executable discovery.

browser_capability.description:
Fresh browser capability for browser-backed flows. Non-browser flows do
not project this field, keeping adapters from inferring OS behavior.

expires_at.description:

entries.connection_model: Provider mail uses a tagged mailbox reference backed by a vault-held service credential. Local draft and template work may not require provider access.
gotchas: Historical drafts and templates cannot resume single-message sending.
A provider acceptance response is not a substitute for declared delivery or thread readback.
If a mail provider call fails, run email.connection.check once and report its status; do not retry the failed call until the check returns ok.
identifier_semantics: Mailbox references, local draft IDs, provider message IDs, and thread IDs are separate domains.
Read history using the canonical thread and message identifiers returned by Email operations.

metadata.summary: Read email history, inbox sync, threads, and connected mailboxes.
metadata.title: Email

entries.purpose: Read recorded mail and synchronize inbound mail. User sending is available only through GmailBulk on the Mail page.

entries.connection_model: Provider work uses a tagged Instagram operator account established by the attended browser login flow.
gotchas: User search returns the native user array without a continuation cursor; inspect selected profiles separately before preparing Creator saves.
Login state can expire and require attended reconnect.
Preserve provider-returned identifiers instead of reconstructing them from display names.
After network_unreachable, run instagram.connection.check once and report its status; do not retry the failed call until the check returns ok.
identifier_semantics: Instagram handles and media locators remain Instagram-specific.
A Creator ID does not replace an Instagram account locator.

metadata.summary: A visual social network centered on creator profiles, photos, Reels, comments, and direct messages.
metadata.title: Instagram

entries.purpose: Find accounts, inspect public profiles and content, and manage the connected operator session.

entries.connection_model: OneCrew records are local. Outreach derives its operator from the selected route or conversation; use each operation's exact input and connection contract.
gotchas: Ask user questions with onecrew.ask_user_question and consume completed answers once. Answers clarify intent; they do not approve an unrelated downstream write.
Do not merge identities from display names alone.
Present result_ref for the user's App confirmation of the held payload without refetching, then read back saved Creators. Choice answers are not save authority.
Each confirmation authorizes one frozen call. Batches reuse result_ref for later reviews and keep completed receipts; only final status resumes the model.
Only onecrew.creator.export XLSX is canonical; map CSV or other sheets into explicit onecrew.creator.batch.create items and reject missing or ambiguous fields.
Owner statuses: eligible_new, eligible_update, existing_skipped, duplicate_skipped, identity_pending, contact_conflict, failed; count eligible_new toward a new Creator target.
identifier_semantics: OneCrew record IDs are durable local identities and are not provider handles.
Candidate explicit intent (add_new/save_or_update), target, connection, provenance, notes, tags and quality; batches use one intent and no candidate cache.
Historical discovery and candidate IDs stay provenance; current reads return provider IDs. Use actual row_id values for reviews and outcomes.
onecrew.creator.candidate.batch.save takes one candidates array, up to 50; the eight-call envelope and provider concurrency are separate limits.
A link hub found in any profile is read with onecrew.link_hub.extract: links and emails return as found; nothing is saved until a Creator save confirms them.
Owner preparation reads fresh profiles and hubs, writes no Creator rows or reservations, and holds the immutable typed payload in the result owner.

metadata.summary: OneCrew's local system for Creators, contact routes, conversations, and outreach history.
metadata.title: onecrew_lite

entries.purpose: Use OneCrew for durable Creator records, reviewed platform saves, confirmed contact routes, historical conversations, classifications, and revision-aware local changes.

entries.connection_model: Provider work uses a tagged Telegram operator account. Login can continue through QR, phone code, OTP, or 2FA steps and may require a configured SOCKS5 proxy.
gotchas: Community search returns native public chat objects without a cursor or Creator snapshot. Use their real IDs and kinds to resolve a community and read administrators.
Administrator reads return a bounded page; a missing member does not prove absence. Prepare selected locators directly and present result_ref for App confirmation.
Continuation codes and passwords are transient secrets and must not be repeated in catalog queries.
After network_unreachable, run telegram.connection.check once and report its status; do not retry the failed call until the check returns ok.
identifier_semantics: Chat, channel, user, and message identifiers are distinct Telegram domains.
Carry identifiers returned by the selected Telegram account rather than guessing usernames.
telegram.community.get and telegram.community.administrators.list use current typed locators and return public data without phone numbers or access hashes.

metadata.summary: A messaging platform organized around private chats, groups, channels, and their administrators.
metadata.title: Telegram

entries.purpose: Find public communities, inspect or resolve community participants, and manage an MTProto operator session.

capability_categories: author discovery through advanced post search
entries.connection_model: Provider work uses a tagged X operator account. Browser login and reconnect are attended lifecycle steps; connection identity remains X-specific.
gotchas: Select x.posts.search.advanced and deduplicate authors before verification.
Read profile or recent posts only when quality or geography evidence is missing; otherwise pass locator, connection and provenance to Creator save preparation.
A post's language is not evidence that its author lives in that language's country. Keep requested geography and content-quality checks in the plan's acceptance criteria.
Search and thread reads return native X pages and cursors without creating Creator records or snapshots. Pass the native next_cursor unchanged to continue.
Do not substitute an Instagram handle or Creator ID for an X locator.
After network_unreachable, run x.connection.check once and report its status; do not retry the failed call until the check returns ok.
identifier_semantics: Handles identify X accounts; preserve the returned spelling when passing them to another X operation.
Post locators and account locators are different identifier domains.

metadata.summary: A public social network for real-time conversations, posts, relationships, and creator profiles.
metadata.title: X

entries.purpose: Find people by searching posts with x.posts.search.advanced and inspecting their authors. Read selected public profiles, recent posts and threads to verify the requested criteria, and manage the operator account lifecycle.

entries.connection_model: Provider reads use a tagged YouTube service credential stored by the local vault; credential setup and rotation are separate lifecycle actions.
gotchas: Search returns native items and next_page_token, at most 50 per page. Repeated videos from one channel stay separate hits; each channel is described once in the channels map.
youtube.channel.get requires depth: light or full. Light omits comments and marks them omitted; full requests comments; unavailable sections mean the attempted read failed.
Read youtube.channel.get only when quality evidence is missing; otherwise pass channel ID, connection and provenance directly to Creator save preparation.
Before verification, deduplicate hits by stable channel ID across connections and read depths. Keep each source and provenance; do not merge names or unresolved handles.
API quota or credential validity can block reads; a channel handle is not a channel ID.
After network_unreachable, run youtube.connection.check once and report its status; do not retry the failed call until the check returns ok.
identifier_semantics: Channel IDs, video IDs, and handles are different locator forms.
Use the locator required by the exact selected operation schema.

directory.connection_model: OneCrew records are local. Outreach derives its operator from the selected route or conversation; use each operation's exact input and connection contract.
gotchas: Ask user questions with onecrew.ask_user_question and consume completed answers once. Answers clarify intent; they do not approve an unrelated downstream write.
Do not merge identities from display names alone.
Present result_ref for the user's App confirmation of the held payload without refetching, then read back saved Creators. Choice answers are not save authority.
Each confirmation authorizes one frozen call. Batches reuse result_ref for later reviews and keep completed receipts; only final status resumes the model.
Only onecrew.creator.export XLSX is canonical; map CSV or other sheets into explicit onecrew.creator.batch.create items and reject missing or ambiguous fields.
Owner statuses: eligible_new, eligible_update, existing_skipped, duplicate_skipped, identity_pending, contact_conflict, failed; count eligible_new toward a new Creator target.
identifier_semantics: OneCrew record IDs are durable local identities and are not provider handles.
Candidate explicit intent (add_new/save_or_update), target, connection, provenance, notes, tags and quality; batches use one intent and no candidate cache.
Historical discovery and candidate IDs stay provenance; current reads return provider IDs. Use actual row_id values for reviews and outcomes.
onecrew.creator.candidate.batch.save takes one candidates array, up to 50; the eight-call envelope and provider concurrency are separate limits.
A link hub found in any profile is read with onecrew.link_hub.extract: links and emails return as found; nothing is saved until a Creator save confirms them.
Owner preparation reads fresh profiles and hubs, writes no Creator rows or reservations, and holds the immutable typed payload in the result owner.

Continuation codes and passwords are transient secrets and must not be repeated in catalog queries.

directory.connection_model: Provider reads use a tagged YouTube service credential stored by the local vault; credential setup and rotation are separate lifecycle actions.
gotchas: Search returns native items and next_page_token, at most 50 per page. Repeated videos from one channel stay separate hits; each channel is described once in the channels map.
youtube.channel.get requires depth: light or full. Light omits comments and marks them omitted; full requests comments; unavailable sections mean the attempted read failed.
Read youtube.channel.get only when quality evidence is missing; otherwise pass channel ID, connection and provenance directly to Creator save preparation.
Before verification, deduplicate hits by stable channel ID across connections and read depths. Keep each source and provenance; do not merge names or unresolved handles.
API quota or credential validity can block reads; a channel handle is not a channel ID.
After network_unreachable, run youtube.connection.check once and report its status; do not retry the failed call until the check returns ok.
identifier_semantics: Channel IDs, video IDs, and handles are different locator forms.
Use the locator required by the exact selected operation schema.

input_schema.description:
The one canonical public sync intent: a mailbox reference and an
explicit bounded mode. Provider cursors never cross a public boundary.

mode.description:
Bounded run modes. `Incremental` is the canonical pull-only run: bounded
newest-first reconciliation plus automatic resumption of an unfinished
historical backfill.

output_schema.description: The result of one coalesced bidirectional sync run.

inbound.description: One direction's share of a completed sync run.

anyOf.description:
Sanitized, resumable failure state for one mailbox direction. Persisted
as JSON in `mailbox_sync_state.failure_json`; carries provider ids and an
error class only — never secrets, URLs, or raw provider payloads.

merged_threads.description:
RFC-proven thread merges performed by imported outbound roots;
always zero for the inbound direction.

reconciled_statuses.description:
Delivery statuses reconciled in place from sent list metadata;
always zero for the inbound direction.

outbound.description: One direction's share of a completed sync run.

anyOf.description:
Sanitized, resumable failure state for one mailbox direction. Persisted
as JSON in `mailbox_sync_state.failure_json`; carries provider ids and an
error class only — never secrets, URLs, or raw provider payloads.

merged_threads.description:
RFC-proven thread merges performed by imported outbound roots;
always zero for the inbound direction.

reconciled_statuses.description:
Delivery statuses reconciled in place from sent list metadata;
always zero for the inbound direction.

pending_triage.description:
一个收件箱欠下的判断:有界的清单加上真实总数,免得积压很多时把
返回撑爆,又不至于让被截断的部分看起来不存在。

items.description:
一条还欠着判断的入站消息:同步把它收进来了,但没有人——也没有
agent——说过它是什么意思。

它跟着同步结果一起返回,因为提醒放在指令里只是请求,放在返回值里
就是事实:agent 必然读到工具调用的结果,而这份清单要么是空的,要么
明摆着还有活没干。判断完再同步一次,清单自己会空掉。

channel.description: Which inbox the judged reply arrived in.

from.description: 发信人,足够让 agent 认出这是谁而不必再取一次。

total.description: 全部欠着的条数,可能大于 items.len()。

output_schema.description:
Idle-time status: whether a run is in flight in this process plus the
durable per-direction facts. Process-only running state stays separate
from durable watermarks by construction.

anyOf.description:
Public projection of one direction's durable sync state. Deliberately
omits provider pagination positions (`newest_provider_message_id`,
`oldest_backfill_cursor`): those are private engine state, not status.

Sanitized, resumable failure state for one mailbox direction. Persisted
as JSON in `mailbox_sync_state.failure_json`; carries provider ids and an
error class only — never secrets, URLs, or raw provider payloads.

Public projection of one direction's durable sync state. Deliberately
omits provider pagination positions (`newest_provider_message_id`,
`oldest_backfill_cursor`): those are private engine state, not status.

Sanitized, resumable failure state for one mailbox direction. Persisted
as JSON in `mailbox_sync_state.failure_json`; carries provider ids and an
error class only — never secrets, URLs, or raw provider payloads.

Live counters of an in-flight run: the direction currently walking and
what this run has listed, fetched, and imported so far. Process-local by
construction — never durable state, never provider cursors — and reset
per direction, so the UI reads "which phase, how far".

estimated_percent.description:
Estimated share (0–100) of the backfill window already walked. The
provider exposes no total count, but the walk moves newest→oldest
through a bounded retention window, so elapsed time-span is an
honest determinate estimate. Absent when no page boundary is known.

progress.description: Present only while `running`: the in-flight run's live counters.

intent.description:
What an inbound reply is actually asking for. Six values, chosen so a
human scanning a list can act on the tag alone: three that want a reply
now, one that closes the thread, one that is noise, and an escape hatch
so an agent is never forced to mislabel.

oneOf.description: Wants to work together; the next move is ours.
Needs something answered before deciding.
Discussing terms — price, scope, timing.
Said no. The thread is closed unless something changes.
Auto-reply, unrelated, or spam.
Real but none of the above; the summary carries the meaning.

triage.description:
The newest verdict on any inbound message of this thread — newest by
when it was judged, not by which message it judges. A later inbound
that nobody has read yet leaves the earlier verdict standing here;
what is still owed is `pending_triage` on the sync result, not the
absence of this field.

operations.title: X post thread

all_words.description: Words that must all occur; each value is one word, or a space-separated phrase compiled in double quotes.

any_words.description: Alternatives compiled as one parenthesized OR group; each value is one word, or a space-separated phrase compiled in double quotes.

confirmed_plan_ref.description: Execute-only; omit from plan scope arguments. Reference issued by the user-confirmed onecrew.search.plan.prepare card.

count.description: Provider page size from 1 through 100; omitted means 20; a confirmed plan freezes it.

cursor.description: Execute-only continuation from next_cursor; omit from plan scopes.

exact_phrase.description: One phrase compiled inside X Web Search double quotes.

exclude_words.description: Words excluded from results; each value is one word, or a space-separated phrase compiled in double quotes.

from_accounts.description: X handles whose posts may match, with or without a leading `@`.

hashtags.description: Hashtag names, with or without a leading `#`.

language.description: Lowercase X Web Search language code such as `en` or `zh-cn`.

links.description: Include links, exclude links, or leave link filtering unset.

mentioning_accounts.description: X handles that matching posts mention, with or without a leading `@`.

min_likes.description: Minimum like count compiled to the X Web operator `min_faves`.

min_reposts.description: Minimum repost count compiled to the X Web operator `min_retweets`.

replies.description: Include replies, exclude replies, or leave reply filtering unset.

result_mode.description: `top` requests X relevance results; `latest` requests recent results.

search_plan_policy.description: Execute-only; omit from plan scope arguments. Set user_requested_direct only when the current user explicitly asks to skip the plan or search directly; never choose it autonomously.

since.description: Gregorian date compiled through X's `since:YYYY-MM-DD` operator.

to_accounts.description: X handles whose replies may match, with or without a leading `@`.

until.description: Gregorian date compiled through X's `until:YYYY-MM-DD` operator.

operations.summary: Find people through matching X posts using typed words, accounts, language, dates, engagement, reply and link criteria. Returns the native advanced-search page with posts, effective query and next_cursor; it creates no Creator snapshots. Use x.profile.get or x.user_posts.list only when the requested quality or geography evidence is missing; otherwise pass a selected locator, connection and real provenance to Creator save preparation without an extra profile read. Post language does not establish author country.
operations.title: Discover X authors through advanced post search

output_schema.description: One live X profile as X returns it.

followers, following, posts, likes, verified, blue_verified,
profile_image_url, viewer_follows, viewer_followed_by, can_dm.

output_schema.description: One native page of a user's posts as X returns it.

page.description:

text, author, metrics, created_at, media, urls) and `next_cursor`.

operations.summary: List one native page of a user's recent X posts, as X returns it. X controls the page size; use the page's next_cursor to continue. No count parameter.

depth.description: The caller must choose whether comments are part of this read.

oneOf.description:

intentionally do not request public comments.

Preserve the complete channel-read behavior, including comments from
the first recent video when available.

channel.description:
The channel with its About-page links, recent videos and public
comments as returned: channel_id, channel_url, title, description,
description_source_url, custom_url, subscriber_count, full descriptions
in bounded recent_videos, public_comments, about_links and unavailable_sections.

intent.description:
What an inbound reply is actually asking for. Six values, chosen so a
human scanning a list can act on the tag alone: three that want a reply
now, one that closes the thread, one that is noise, and an escape hatch
so an agent is never forced to mislabel.

oneOf.description: Wants to work together; the next move is ours.
Needs something answered before deciding.
Discussing terms — price, scope, timing.
Said no. The thread is closed unless something changes.
Auto-reply, unrelated, or spam.
Real but none of the above; the summary carries the meaning.

triage.description:
The newest verdict on any inbound message of this conversation —
newest by when it was judged, not by which message it judges. A later
unread inbound leaves the earlier verdict standing; what is still owed
is `pending_triage`. It belongs on the row because that is where a
human decides what to open next.

capability_categories: author discovery through advanced post search
directory.connection_model: Provider work uses a tagged X operator account. Browser login and reconnect are attended lifecycle steps; connection identity remains X-specific.
gotchas: Select x.posts.search.advanced and deduplicate authors before verification.
Read profile or recent posts only when quality or geography evidence is missing; otherwise pass locator, connection and provenance to Creator save preparation.
A post's language is not evidence that its author lives in that language's country. Keep requested geography and content-quality checks in the plan's acceptance criteria.
Search and thread reads return native X pages and cursors without creating Creator records or snapshots. Pass the native next_cursor unchanged to continue.
Do not substitute an Instagram handle or Creator ID for an X locator.
After network_unreachable, run x.connection.check once and report its status; do not retry the failed call until the check returns ok.
identifier_semantics: Handles identify X accounts; preserve the returned spelling when passing them to another X operation.
Post locators and account locators are different identifier domains.

directory.purpose: Find people by searching posts with x.posts.search.advanced and inspecting their authors. Read selected public profiles, recent posts and threads to verify the requested criteria, and manage the operator account lifecycle.
directory.summary: A public social network for real-time conversations, posts, relationships, and creator profiles.
directory.title: X

directory.connection_model: Provider reads use a tagged YouTube service credential stored by the local vault; credential setup and rotation are separate lifecycle actions.
gotchas: Search returns native items and next_page_token, at most 50 per page. Repeated videos from one channel stay separate hits; each channel is described once in the channels map.
youtube.channel.get requires depth: light or full. Light omits comments and marks them omitted; full requests comments; unavailable sections mean the attempted read failed.
Read youtube.channel.get only when quality evidence is missing; otherwise pass channel ID, connection and provenance directly to Creator save preparation.
Before verification, deduplicate hits by stable channel ID across connections and read depths. Keep each source and provenance; do not merge names or unresolved handles.
API quota or credential validity can block reads; a channel handle is not a channel ID.
After network_unreachable, run youtube.connection.check once and report its status; do not retry the failed call until the check returns ok.
identifier_semantics: Channel IDs, video IDs, and handles are different locator forms.
Use the locator required by the exact selected operation schema.

items.description:
Supported demo requires first-hand actions/results in saved transcript, not a title,
advertisement, list, third-party retelling or mere tool mention. Text is not visual proof.
Supported tool requires an author-observed link and a successful target-page quotation.
Language requires exact saved author text; spoken language requires transcript.
MatchFit is optional: excellent = strong relevant evidence and an advantage;
good = clear supported relevance; medium = partial fit with a limitation;
low = a cited significant weakness. Missing optional data never lowers fit.
Fit cannot override required eligibility. Unknown fit has insufficient outcome
and no match_level. Absence in one sample cannot reject the whole creator.

directory.connection_model: OneCrew records are local. Outreach derives its operator from the selected route or conversation; use each operation's exact input and connection contract.
gotchas: Ask user questions with onecrew.ask_user_question and consume completed answers once. Answers clarify intent; they do not approve an unrelated downstream write.
Do not merge identities from display names alone.

now, one that closes the thread, one that is noise, and an escape hatch
so an agent is never forced to mislabel.

human decides what to open next.
